description: CallCompass MVP - a demo app showing how NeuDecide (43 MB on-device speech-to-tool-call model, ONNX/CPU via the neudecide Python package) guides a sales agent through a decision tree from one recorded customer utterance. FastAPI backend, vanilla JS frontend, tree defined in a single JSON config, SSE-streamed node-by-node traversal, full run under 1 second on laptop CPU. Full PRD at tasks/prd-callcompass-mvp.md.

userStories.title: Repository scaffold and quality checks
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a runnable project skeleton with quality checks wired up so that every later story can be verified before commit.
acceptanceCriteria: Create repo layout: backend/ (Python package callcompass), frontend/, config/
backend/pyproject.toml declares runtime deps: fastapi, uvicorn[standard], neudecide, onnxruntime, numpy, pydantic
backend/pyproject.toml declares dev deps: ruff, mypy, pytest, httpx
backend/callcompass/main.py exposes a FastAPI app that starts with `uvicorn callcompass.main:app`
ruff check . passes with no errors
mypy backend/callcompass passes with no errors
pytest runs and collects at least one passing placeholder test
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Foundation story. Python 3.11+. Establishes the quality-check commands every later story must run: ruff check, mypy, pytest. Record those exact commands in a CLAUDE.md so later iterations do not have to rediscover them.

userStories.title: Tree config schema, Pydantic models, and validating loader
userStories.description: As a demo operator, I want the decision tree defined in one JSON file so that I can change the sales flow without touching code.
acceptanceCriteria: Pydantic models in backend/callcompass/tree.py implement the Tree Config Schema from the PRD (tree_id, version, product, root, nodes map; branch nodes have options with tool_name/description/argument{name,enum,description}/next; leaf nodes have recommendation and optional rationale)
Loader rejects an argument spec that has no non-empty `enum` list (enum-only arguments are enforced structurally)
Loader rejects a config that declares a tool_name of `none_of_these` (that tool is backend-injected, never configured)

Validation rejects each of: duplicate node ids, a node whose id does not match its map key, a `next` pointer to a missing node id, a branch node with zero options, a leaf without `recommendation`, a cycle, a root id absent from `nodes`, duplicate tool_name within one node
Validation failure raises a single-line error naming the offending node id
config/tree.json contains the complete `northbeam-saas-v1` sample tree from the PRD verbatim, including the level-2 short-circuit leaf `rec_graceful_exit`
Unit tests cover one valid tree plus at least four distinct invalid trees (missing next pointer, duplicate id, cycle, empty options)
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Copy the sample tree JSON exactly from the PRD's 'Sample Tree Config' section. Note the tree is NOT uniform depth: rec_graceful_exit is a level-2 leaf reached after one inference. Every later story must handle varying depth.

userStories.title: Load NeuDecide once at startup with warmup and health endpoint
userStories.description: As a demo operator, I want the model loaded a single time when the server boots so that no request pays model-load cost.
acceptanceCriteria: Model is loaded in a FastAPI lifespan handler and stored on app.state; it is never constructed per request
Startup logs model load duration in ms and confirms the CPU/ONNX execution provider
A warmup inference runs at startup against a short silent audio buffer so the first real request is not cold
GET /api/health returns {"status":"ok","model_loaded":true,"model_load_ms":<int>,"tree_id":"<id>","node_count":<int>}
Tree config is loaded and validated at startup via US-002's loader; an invalid tree fails startup with the single-line error
Server fails fast with a readable message if the model cannot be loaded
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Confirm the real neudecide API before writing this: constructor signature, and whether generate() accepts a file path, raw bytes, or a NumPy float array (PRD Open Questions 1-3). If generate() is not thread-safe, guard it with a lock or a single-worker executor. Record what you find in backend/callcompass/CLAUDE.md - US-004 and US-005 depend on it.

userStories.title: Node-to-tools conversion function
userStories.description: As a developer, I need each branch node converted into the model's tool format so that the model picks from exactly that node's options.
acceptanceCriteria: A pure function converts one branch node into the tool list passed to model.generate(audio, tools)
Function performs no model, network, or filesystem calls
Every generated tool list includes a synthetic `none_of_these` tool with no required arguments
Each node option becomes a tool whose named argument is an enum constrained to exactly that option's declared values
Unit tests assert the exact tool-list shape for the sample tree's `intent` root node and for the mid-tree `signal_check` node
Unit test asserts `none_of_these` is present in every node's tool list across the whole sample tree
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Keep this isolated in ONE file. The PRD flags (R-6) that the assumed neudecide tool-schema shape may not match the shipped package; isolating conversion here makes an API mismatch a single-file change.

userStories.title: Traversal engine with fake-model tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a traversal engine that walks the tree over one audio buffer so that the traversal logic is testable without HTTP or a browser.
acceptanceCriteria: traverse(audio, tree, model) yields one step record per generate() call with fields: node_id, node_label, tool_called, arguments, latency_ms, next_node_id
The same audio buffer is passed at every node (no re-recording, no slicing)
Traversal terminates as `completed` on reaching a leaf, emitting the leaf recommendation and rationale
Traversal terminates as `unplaced` with reason `none_of_these`, `empty_response`, `unknown_tool`, or `depth_limit`
A hard depth cap of 10 steps prevents runaway traversal
latency_ms measures only the generate() call, via time.perf_counter
Unit tests with a fake scripted model cover: full happy path to a leaf, none_of_these at level 1, empty response mid-tree, unknown tool name, the level-2 short-circuit via not_interested
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implement as a generator so US-007 can stream steps as they occur. The fake model (scripted list of responses) is the key test fixture - put it somewhere reusable, US-007's integration test needs it too.

userStories.title: Audio validation and WAV decode
userStories.description: As a developer, I need uploaded audio validated and decoded so that bad input produces a clear 4xx instead of a model crash.
acceptanceCriteria: Accepts WAV upload at 16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM and decodes to the array shape neudecide expects

Rejects with HTTP 400 and a specific message naming the actual value for each of: wrong sample rate, more than one channel, non-WAV payload, duration over 30 seconds, duration under 0.3 seconds, body over 2 MB
Example rejection message format: "Audio must be 16000 Hz mono; received 44100 Hz stereo."
A 1-second 16 kHz mono WAV fixture is generated in tests and decodes successfully
Unit tests cover at least three distinct rejection cases
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Decode shape must match what US-003 established about generate()'s expected audio input. A checked-in or test-generated fixture WAV lets the backend be tested without a browser - the PRD calls this out as mitigation for R-5.

userStories.title: SSE traversal endpoint and GET /api/tree
userStories.description: As a frontend developer, I want traversal results streamed per node so that the UI can light up each node at the moment its inference actually returns.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/analyze accepts multipart/form-data with an `audio` WAV file and responds text/event-stream
Emits events in order: `started`, one `step` per node, exactly one terminal event (`completed` or `unplaced`), then `done`
Event payloads match the PRD's API Endpoints schemas exactly (field names and types)
`completed` includes leaf_node_id, label, recommendation, rationale, path, inference_count, total_inference_ms, total_latency_ms
`unplaced` includes stopped_at_node_id, stopped_at_label, reason, path, inference_count, total_inference_ms, total_latency_ms
Audio rejection from US-006 returns HTTP 400 JSON before the stream opens
A mid-stream exception emits an `error` event with a message and node_id, then `done`; the connection is never left hanging
Synchronous CPU inference runs in a thread executor so the event loop is not blocked
GET /api/tree returns the validated tree config verbatim
Integration test with httpx and the fake model asserts the full event sequence for the happy path and for the unplaced path
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Last backend story - after this the API surface is complete and all remaining work is frontend. `done` must always be the final event, including after `error`.

userStories.title: Frontend shell served by FastAPI
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a static frontend shell served from the same process so that the demo runs on one port with no build step.
acceptanceCriteria: FastAPI serves frontend/ as static files; GET / returns the page
Page is vanilla HTML/CSS/JS using ES modules, with no bundler and no build step
Three-column layout renders per the PRD screen layout: Capture (~25%), Tree (~50%), Trace (~25%), with a result area below the tree spanning the center and right columns
Dark background styling suitable for projection; latency figures styled in monospace
Columns contain labelled empty placeholders; no behaviour is wired up yet
Page calls GET /api/health on load and shows a visible inline error if the backend is not ready
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Pure layout and plumbing story - no recording, no tree rendering, no SSE. Existing only so later UI stories have a page to attach to. Confirm with dev-browser that all three columns and the result area are visible at laptop width.

userStories.title: Browser audio capture and 16 kHz mono WAV encoding
userStories.description: As a sales agent, I want my recording converted to the exact format the backend needs so that the model receives valid audio.
acceptanceCriteria: getUserMedia captures microphone audio on button press
Captured audio is converted to 16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM with a valid WAV header, entirely client-side
Uses AudioContext at 16 kHz where supported, otherwise resamples in an AudioWorklet
The encoded WAV bytes are retained in memory for both upload and playback (same bytes for both)
POSTing the encoded WAV to /api/analyze is accepted by US-006's validation (no HTTP 400)
Denied or unavailable microphone shows an inline message in the Capture column - never alert() and never a silent failure
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: The highest-risk frontend story (PRD R-5): a subtly wrong WAV header or sample rate produces confidently wrong model output rather than an error. Verify acceptance by actually POSTing to the live backend and confirming no 400. Target Chrome/Edge.

userStories.title: Record/stop button with live waveform and timer
userStories.description: As a sales agent, I want to record a customer utterance with visible feedback so that I know the mic is live and how long I have left.
acceptanceCriteria: A single circular button toggles Record to Stop, with a visually distinct recording state (red pulse)
A live waveform renders on a Canvas from Web Audio API analyser data while recording
Waveform sits flat and gray when idle
A timer counts up and displays the 30-second ceiling, e.g. "0:12 / 0:30"
Recording auto-stops at exactly 30 seconds
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Builds the UI on top of US-009's capture pipeline. Split from capture deliberately so the audio-format work and the visual work can each be verified on their own.

userStories.title: Recording playback control
userStories.description: As a sales agent, I want to play back what I just recorded so that I can confirm the audio the model actually heard.
acceptanceCriteria: After stopping, a play/pause control plus an elapsed-time readout appears in the Capture column
Playback uses the same WAV bytes that are sent to the backend
Control is disabled and grayed (not hidden) before any recording exists
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Playback is a demo-operator diagnostic for PRD risk R-1: it is how the operator confirms what the model actually received after a misfire. Must use the encoded bytes, not a separate MediaRecorder blob.

userStories.title: Static tree visualization from config
userStories.description: As a demo viewer, I want to see the whole decision tree before anything runs so that I understand the space the model is choosing within.
acceptanceCriteria: Tree is fetched from GET /api/tree on page load and rendered as an inline SVG node graph, levels laid out top to bottom
Every node shows its label; leaf nodes use a distinct shape and accent color from branch nodes
All nodes start dimmed at low opacity with a thin border ("not visited" state)
Layout is computed at render time from node depth and sibling index, with no hardcoded node coordinates
Renders the non-uniform sample tree correctly, including the level-2 leaf rec_graceful_exit
Editing a node label in config/tree.json and restarting the server changes the rendering with no code edit
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: No hardcoded positions - this is what makes PRD AC-10 (re-point the demo by editing JSON only) true. Verify the uneven-depth case renders sanely, since rec_graceful_exit sits at level 2 while its siblings' subtrees reach level 4.

userStories.title: Live path highlighting and trace panel from SSE
userStories.description: As a demo viewer, I want each node to light up as its inference returns so that I can see the traversal happening in real time.
acceptanceCriteria: On stop, the frontend POSTs the WAV to /api/analyze and consumes the SSE stream via fetch + ReadableStream (not EventSource, which cannot POST a file body)
Each `step` event lights its node and draws the edge from its parent, in arrival order
Each lit node displays the option picked, the argument name and value, and latency_ms
A step card is appended to the Trace column per step: node label header, option picked in bold, argument as name: value in monospace, right-aligned latency badge
A running total (e.g. "Total: 384 ms") is pinned at the top of the Trace column and updates per step
Node highlight transitions are approximately 120 ms
Record button is disabled while a traversal is in flight
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: The centerpiece story. Nodes must light on actual event arrival - no artificial delays, since real per-call timing is the thing being demonstrated. Verify with a real recording end to end against the live backend.

userStories.title: Recommendation leaf card
userStories.description: As a sales agent, I want the final recommendation in plain language so that I know what to say next.
acceptanceCriteria: On `completed`, a green-accented card renders in the result area with the leaf recommendation text at large readable size
Card shows the path taken as a readable breadcrumb of chosen options, e.g. "Pricing question -> Pro tier -> Budget objection"
Card shows total end-to-end latency in ms in monospace
Card renders only after the terminal event, never mid-traversal
Rationale is shown in smaller text beneath the recommendation
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Breadcrumb shows chosen OPTION labels, not node labels (PRD Open Question 5 - option labels read better and were the assumption).

userStories.title: Couldn't place this state
userStories.description: As a demo viewer, I want an explicit failure state so that the demo is honest when the model declines to choose.
acceptanceCriteria: On `unplaced`, an amber-accented card reads "Couldn't place this" in the result area
Card names the node where traversal stopped and the reason in plain language (none of these / empty response / unrecognized tool / depth limit)
Nodes visited before the stop remain lit
The unresolved node takes a distinct warning outline, visually different from both visited and unvisited nodes
No recommendation text is shown in this state
An `error` event renders a recoverable UI state, not a hung spinner
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Verify by recording genuinely off-topic audio (e.g. weather chat) against the live backend, not just by mocking the event. PRD AC-8 requires the real path.

userStories.title: Reset button
userStories.description: As a demo operator, I want a one-click reset so that I can run the demo repeatedly in front of an audience.
acceptanceCriteria: A secondary Reset button at the bottom of the Capture column clears the recording, playback control, all node highlighting, the Trace column, and any result card
Tree returns to its fully dimmed initial state without a page reload
Reset is enabled after both `completed` and `unplaced`, and is disabled before any run has finished
Reset cancels any in-flight SSE stream
Two consecutive runs produce correct, non-accumulating results (trace cards do not stack up from the previous run)
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: Verify the non-accumulation criterion explicitly: run, reset, run again, and confirm the Trace column and total latency reflect only the second run.

userStories.title: README with setup, tree editing guide, and demo script
userStories.description: As a colleague who did not build this, I want documentation so that I can run the demo without asking a question.
acceptanceCriteria: README.md documents install and run commands verified from a clean checkout
README documents how to edit config/tree.json, including the full schema and the constraints the loader enforces
README includes a suggested demo script with at least one example utterance per level-1 branch (pricing_question, feature_question, not_interested)
README includes one example off-topic utterance expected to produce the "couldn't place this" state
README states the single-utterance scope and the explicit non-goals (no live multi-turn calls, no CRM, English only, no speaker demographics) so the demo is not over-read as a product
README documents the measured median and p95 total latency over 20 runs
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Covers PRD AC-20 and mitigates R-1 (a pre-verified demo script) and R-7 (demo over-read as a product). The latency figures must be measured, not estimated - run the 20 runs and record the real numbers.
